From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 14:03:00 +0000
Subject: Kickoff: support & SLA onboarding checklist request — SkylineCloud

Hi Sam,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood. Procurement asked me to kick off the vendor setup and confirmation of support/SLA details ahead of PO issuance. To keep procurement and legal moving, could you please complete the attached Vendor_Onboarding_Form.pdf and review the Redwood_Support-SLA_Template.xlsx I’ve attached with our standard fields populated. Specifically we need:  

- Primary support contact (name/email/phone)
- 24x7 escalation contact for Sev1 incidents
- Typical response and resolution targets by severity (P1/P2/P3)
- Any blackout windows or planned maintenance notices you require us to know about
- Confirmation of uptime SLOs you can commit to for the hosted model (monthly uptime %)
- Invoicing contact and PO process notes (billing email, net terms)

Timeline: procurement needs completed forms + basic SLA answers by EOD Friday (2026-12-11) so we can attach to the PO. If anything here is a blocker, flag it and we’ll route for expedited review.

Attachments: Vendor_Onboarding_Form.pdf (form), Redwood_Support-SLA_Template.xlsx (template)

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Vendor Programs Manager | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

Subject: Re: Kickoff: support & SLA onboarding checklist request — SkylineCloud

Hi Olga —

Appreciate the clear list. I’ve attached a completed Vendor_Onboarding_Form (see inline answers) and answered the SLA template where we can. A couple of clarifying points:  

1) Uptime commitment: we can offer a 99.95% monthly uptime SLO for the API endpoints that will back your Dedicated offering; for edge CDN-cached content the SLO is 99.9%. Is Redwood able to accept a split SLO for different classes of endpoints?
2) Escalation path: we have a 24x7 on-call rotation for Sev1. Primary on-call is Marta (marta.gonzalez@skylinecloud.com) — I’ll provide direct mobile for legal/PO exchange only.
3) Billing/PO: our finance team prefers a single annual PO. We can accept NET30 and will route invoices to procure_ops@acmeprocure.com (that’s our AP SaaS aggregator). Is Redwood’s billing team OK with a consolidated annual invoice?

We’re happy to hop on a short call if you want to align on exact endpoints and tags for the SLO split. Proposed next steps in this thread: Marcus from your side confirm acceptance of split SLO and Lauren to confirm PO process for consolidated invoice.

Best,
Sam
Director, Cloud Partnerships — SkylineCloud
sam.rodriguez@skylinecloud.com
[Attachment: Vendor_Onboarding_Form-completed.pdf (pdf, 210KB)]

Morning all —

Thanks Sam, that all looks reasonable. A few internal clarifications from the ops side:  

- Redwood can accept a split SLO by endpoint class. For contract and alerting purposes we’ll tag the API endpoints that carry production inference traffic as Premium (99.95% SLO) and Caching/edge assets as Standard (99.9% SLO).
- Escalation chain we expect to see in the vendor contact list: Primary on-call (name/email/mobile), Secondary on-call, and an executive escalation (VP/Head level) for SLA disputes. Please include estimated MTTR for P1 and P2.
- Our standard target response/resolution buckets (please confirm you can meet or better):
  - P1 (Sev1) — Response within 15 mins, remediation comms within 1 hour, work-around or full recovery target 4 hours
  - P2 — Response within 1 hour, remediation comms within 4 hours, recovery target 48 hours
  - P3 — Response within 8 business hours, recovery target 5 business days

Lauren — for the consolidated annual PO, do we need any additional vendor paperwork (W-9, SOW) or is the onboarding form and signed SLA sufficient? If AP needs vendor taxonomy mapping let me know.

Marcus Lin
Head of Production Operations | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
